- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate during periods of sustained high prices; adjust upward if recent history shows persistent elevated levels.
- Lag in response to true price drops — model often fails to recognize sharp declines until later; apply early correction for sudden drops.
- Overshoot after price spikes — model tends to overreact and forecast higher than true outcome; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak observed price.
- Mean reversion bias — model holds onto high forecasts longer than true price reverts; reduce forecast slope after 3–5 consecutive high values.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate low-price periods; adjust downward if recent 7–14 day average is below 30-day average.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — if last 5–7 days show strong volatility, don’t extrapolate linearly; use smoothing or decay-weighted average.
